SWIPE ▸

cards.p: Write a quote text for a [beds] bed, [baths] bath home: price [price], what is included, how long it takes.
Explain a regular clean versus a deep clean in 4 short lines so a new client picks the right one.
Write a move out clean quote: price [price], what we clean inside cabinets and appliances, and what we skip.
Write 8 questions for an office walkthrough before I quote: size, foot traffic, restrooms, hours, supplies, access.
A one time client loved the clean. Write a short text offering a [weekly or biweekly] slot at [price].
Write a text asking a new client how we get in: key, code or someone home. Ask about pets and parking.
Write a calm text telling [client] my team is [minutes] late, the new arrival time, and a short sorry.
We arrived and could not get in. Write a polite text with my lockout fee [fee] and two rebooking times.
A client says we missed [area]. Write a text that thanks them and offers a free reclean within [days].
Write the day before text for clients: clear counters, secure pets, tell us about any problem areas.
Turn these client notes into a short card my team reads before each visit: [paste notes]. Bullet points only.
We broke [item] at a client's home. Write an honest text: what happened, sorry, and how we make it right.
Write a text for two hours after a clean: thank them, ask for honest feedback, share my review link [link].
Turn this 5 star review into a short note I can read to my cleaners at our next meeting: [paste].
Reply calmly to this review saying the house was not clean: [paste]. Offer a reclean. Under 60 words.
A review has photos of our work: [paste]. Write a thank you reply and ask to repost them.
I have one photo of a sparkling [room]. Plan Monday to Friday posts around it, each a different angle.
Write 5 quick tips a client can do in [room] between our visits. One line each, for a carousel.
Write a post busting 3 common cleaning myths, one line each, plain words, ending with how to book us.
Write a post for a [season] deep clean: what is included, open dates [dates], and how to grab a spot.
Sort these receipts into supplies, gas, equipment, wages, other: [paste]. Total each. Flag any I cannot place.
Write a polite text to [client] that the [date] clean for [amount] is still unpaid. Add my pay link [link].
Ask regular clients by text to set up autopay with [app] so each clean gets paid on time.
Using [supplies, gas, hours, pay], show my cost per clean and what is left at [price].
